sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ṣaṭtriṃśe tv atha saṃprāpte varṣe kauravanandanaḥ dadarśa viparītāni nimittāni yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the thirty-sixth year had come, Yudhiṣṭhira, joy of the Kurus, beheld portents of an evil and contrary kind.

sanskrit: vavur vātāḥ sanirghātā rūkṣāḥ śarkaravarṣiṇaḥ apasavyāni śakunā maṇḍalāni pracakrire
english: Harsh winds blew, attended by thunderclaps and showers of gravel, and the birds wheeled in their circling flights from the left.

sanskrit: pratyagūhur mahānadyo diśo nīhārasaṃvṛtāḥ ulkāś cāṅgāravarṣiṇyaḥ prapetur gaganād bhuvi
english: The great rivers ran backward against their course, the quarters of the sky were wrapped in mist, and meteors raining live coals fell from the heavens upon the earth.

sanskrit: ādityo rajasā rājan samavacchannamaṇḍalaḥ viraśmir udaye nityaṃ kabandhaiḥ samadṛśyata
english: O king, the sun's orb was veiled with dust; rayless at its rising day after day, it was seen ringed about by headless trunks.

sanskrit: pariveṣāś ca dṛśyante dāruṇāḥ candrasūryayoḥ trivarṇāḥ śyāmarūkṣāntās tathā bhasmāruṇaprabhāḥ
english: Dreadful halos appeared about both the moon and the sun, of three colors, dark and rough at their edges, and glowing with an ashen-red light.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahava utpātā bhayaśaṃsinaḥ dṛśyante 'har aho rājan hṛdayodvegakārakāḥ
english: These and many other portents foretelling terror were seen day after day, O king, casting the heart into agitation.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śuśrāva vṛṣṇicakrasya mausale kadanaṃ kṛtam
english: Then, after some time had passed, Yudhiṣṭhira, king of the Kurus, heard that the host of the Vṛṣṇis had been destroyed in the slaughter of the iron clubs.

sanskrit: vimuktaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca śrutvā rāmaṃ ca pāṇḍavaḥ samānīyābravīd bhrātṝn kiṃ kariṣyāma ity uta
english: And hearing that Vāsudeva and Rāma had departed from their bodies, the son of Pāṇḍu gathered his brothers and said to them, "What now shall we do?"

sanskrit: parasparaṃ samāsādya brahmadaṇḍabalātkṛtān vṛṣṇīn vinaṣṭāṃs te śrutvā vyathitāḥ pāṇḍavābhavan
english: When they heard how the Vṛṣṇis, driven on by the force of a brahmin's curse, had fallen upon one another and perished, the Pāṇḍavas were stricken with grief.

sanskrit: nidhanaṃ vāsudevasya samudrasyeva śoṣaṇam vīrā na śraddadhus tasya vināśaṃ śārṅgadhanvanaḥ
english: The death of Vāsudeva was like the drying up of the ocean; those heroes could not believe in the destruction of him who bore the Śārṅga bow.

sanskrit: mausalaṃ te pariśrutya duḥkhaśokasamanvitāḥ viṣaṇṇā hatasaṃkalpāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ samupāviśan
english: Having heard of the affair of the clubs, the Pāṇḍavas, filled with grief and sorrow, despondent and bereft of all resolve, sat down together.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ vinaṣṭā bhagavann andhakā vṛṣṇibhiḥ saha paśyato vāsudevasya bhojāś caiva mahārathāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: How, holy one, did the Andhakas perish together with the Vṛṣṇis, and the Bhojas, those great chariot-warriors, while Vāsudeva looked on?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ṣaṭtriṃśe 'tha tato varṣe vṛṣṇīnām anayo mahān anyonyaṃ musalais te tu nijaghnuḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: In the thirty-sixth year a great calamity befell the Vṛṣṇis, and, driven on by Time, they slew one another with iron clubs.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kenānuśaptās te vīrāḥ kṣayaṃ vṛṣṇyandhakā yayuḥ bhojāś ca dvijavarya tvaṃ vistareṇa vadasva me
english: Janamejaya said: By whom were those heroes cursed, that the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas met their ruin, and the Bhojas too? Best of the twice-born, tell me this in full.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca viśvāmitraṃ ca kaṇvaṃ ca nāradaṃ ca tapodhanam sāraṇapramukhā vīrā dadṛśur dvārakāgatān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The heroes, with Sāraṇa at their head, saw Viśvāmitra, Kaṇva, and Nārada, that treasury of austerities, who had come to Dvārakā.

sanskrit: te vai sāmbaṃ puraskṛtya bhūṣayitvā striyaṃ yathā abruvann upasaṃgamya daivadaṇḍanipīḍitāḥ
english: Then, putting Sāmba forward, decked out like a woman, they approached the sages and, oppressed by the rod of destiny, addressed them thus:

sanskrit: iyaṃ strī putrakāmasya babhror amitatejasaḥ ṛṣayaḥ sādhu jānīta kim iyaṃ janayiṣyati
english: "This woman is the wife of Babhru of boundless splendor, who longs for a son. O seers, divine it truly: what will she bring forth?"

sanskrit: ity uktās te tadā rājan vipralambhapradharṣitāḥ pratyabruvaṃs tān munayo yat tac chṛṇu narādhipa
english: Thus addressed, O king, the sages, outraged at being so deceived, answered them; hear what they said, lord of men.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇyandhakavināśāya musalaṃ ghoram āyasam vāsudevasya dāyādaḥ sāmbo 'yaṃ janayiṣyati
english: "For the destruction of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, this Sāmba, heir of Vāsudeva, will bring forth a terrible iron club,

sanskrit: yena yūyaṃ sudurvṛttā nṛśaṃsā jātamanyavaḥ ucchettāraḥ kulaṃ kṛtsnam ṛte rāmajanārdanau
english: by which you, vicious, cruel, and full of wrath, will utterly root out your whole race, save only Rāma and Janārdana.

sanskrit: samudraṃ yāsyati śrīmāṃs tyaktvā dehaṃ halāyudhaḥ jarā kṛṣṇaṃ mahātmānaṃ śayānaṃ bhuvi bhetsyati
english: The glorious Halāyudha, casting off his body, will go to the sea; and one named Jara will pierce the great-souled Kṛṣṇa as he lies upon the ground."

sanskrit: ity abruvanta te rājan pralabdhās tair durātmabhiḥ munayaḥ krodharaktākṣāḥ samīkṣyātha parasparam
english: So spoke the sages, O king, mocked by those evil-minded men, their eyes red with anger as they glanced at one another.

sanskrit: tathoktvā munayas te tu tataḥ keśavam abhyayuḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the sages then went to Keśava.

sanskrit: athābravīt tadā vṛṣṇīñ śrutvaivaṃ madhusūdanaḥ antajño matimāṃs tasya bhavitavyaṃ tatheti tān
english: Then the slayer of Madhu, hearing of this, spoke to the Vṛṣṇis; wise and knowing the end, he told them, "What is fated must be so."

sanskrit: evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaḥ praviveśa punar gṛhān kṛtāntam anyathā naicchat kartuṃ sa jagataḥ prabhuḥ
english: Having said this, Hṛṣīkeśa went again into his house; for the lord of the world had no wish to turn fate to another course.

sanskrit: śvobhūte 'tha tataḥ sāmbo musalaṃ tad asūta vai vṛṣṇyandhakavināśāya kiṃkarapratimaṃ mahat
english: On the morrow Sāmba indeed brought forth that club, great as a death-dealing servant of Yama, for the destruction of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas.

sanskrit: prasūtaṃ śāpajaṃ ghoraṃ tac ca rājñe nyavedayan viṣaṇṇarūpas tad rājā sūkṣmaṃ cūrṇam akārayat
english: They reported to the king the birth of that dread thing, the offspring of the curse; and the king, downcast of face, had it ground to fine powder.

sanskrit: prākṣipan sāgare tac ca puruṣā rājaśāsanāt aghoṣayaṃś ca nagare vacanād āhukasya ca
english: By the king's command men cast it into the sea, and at the word of Āhuka they proclaimed throughout the city:

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti sarveṣu vṛṣṇyandhakagṛheṣv iha surāsavo na kartavyaḥ sarvair nagaravāsibhiḥ
english: "From this day forward, in all the houses of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, no spirituous drink shall be made by any dweller of this city.

sanskrit: yaś ca no 'viditaṃ kuryāt peyaṃ kaś cin naraḥ kva cit jīvan sa śūlam ārohet svayaṃ kṛtvā sabāndhavaḥ
english: And whatever man shall make strong drink anywhere unknown to us, he shall be impaled alive upon a stake of his own making, together with his kinsmen."

sanskrit: tato rājabhayāt sarve niyamaṃ cakrire tadā narāḥ śāsanam ājñāya tasya rājño mahātmanaḥ
english: Then, out of fear of the king, all men bound themselves to this rule, having learned the command of that great-souled monarch.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ prayatamānānāṃ vṛṣṇīnām andhakaiḥ saha kālo gṛhāṇi sarveṣāṃ paricakrāma nityaśaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the Vṛṣṇis, together with the Andhakas, strove thus, Time prowled about the houses of them all, day after day.

sanskrit: karālo vikaṭo muṇḍaḥ puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalaḥ gṛhāṇy avekṣya vṛṣṇīnāṃ nādṛśyata punaḥ kva cit
english: A man hideous, misshapen, and bald, dark and tawny of hue, would peer into the houses of the Vṛṣṇis and then be seen no more anywhere.

sanskrit: utpedire mahāvātā dāruṇāś cā dine dine vṛṣṇyandhakavināśāya bahavo romaharṣaṇāḥ
english: Day after day great and terrible winds arose, hair-raising and many in number, for the destruction of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas.

sanskrit: vivṛddhamūṣakā rathyā vibhinnamaṇikās tathā cīcīkūcīti vāśyantyaḥ sārikā vṛṣṇiveśmasu nopaśāmyati śabdaś ca sa divārātram eva hi
english: The streets swarmed with rats, the earthen pots cracked apart, and the mynah birds cried "cīcī-kūcī" in the dwellings of the Vṛṣṇis; nor did that clamor cease either by day or by night.

sanskrit: anukurvann ulūkānāṃ sārasā virutaṃ tathā ajāḥ śivānāṃ ca rutam anvakurvata bhārata
english: The cranes mimicked the hooting of owls, and the goats, O Bhārata, took up the howling of jackals.

sanskrit: pāṇḍurā raktapādāś ca vihagāḥ kālacoditāḥ vṛṣṇyandhakānāṃ geheṣu kapotā vyacaraṃs tadā
english: Pale birds with red feet, driven on by Time—pigeons—then roamed about within the houses of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas.

sanskrit: vyajāyanta kharā goṣu karabhāśvatarīṣu ca śunīṣv api biḍālāś ca mūṣakā nakulīṣu ca
english: Asses were born of cattle, and camels of she-mules; cats were born of bitches, and rats of mongooses.

sanskrit: nāpatrapanta pāpāni kurvanto vṛṣṇayas tadā prādviṣan brāhmaṇāṃś cāpi pitṝn devāṃs tathaiva ca
english: The Vṛṣṇis, working evil, then knew no shame; they came to hate even the brahmins, the ancestors, and the gods alike.

sanskrit: gurūṃś cāpy avamanyanta na tu rāmajanārdanau patnyaḥ patīn vyuccaranta patnīś ca patayas tathā
english: They scorned their elders too—though not Rāma and Janārdana; wives wronged their husbands, and husbands their wives.

sanskrit: vibhāvasuḥ prajvalito vāmaṃ viparivartate nīlalohitamāñjiṣṭhā visṛjann arciṣaḥ pṛthak
english: The blazing fire, when kindled, turned to the left, sending forth its flames apart in hues of blue, blood-red, and madder.

sanskrit: udayāstamane nityaṃ puryāṃ tasyāṃ divākaraḥ vyadṛśyatāsakṛt puṃbhiḥ kabandhaiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: At rising and at setting, day after day in that city, the sun was seen by men again and again ringed about by headless trunks.

sanskrit: mahānaseṣu siddhe 'nne saṃskṛte 'tīva bhārata āhāryamāṇe kṛmayo vyadṛśyanta narādhipa
english: In the kitchens, when the food was cooked and most carefully prepared, worms were seen in it as it was being served, O lord of men.

sanskrit: puṇyāhe vācyamāne ca japatsu ca mahātmasu abhidhāvantaḥ śrūyante na cādṛśyata kaś cana
english: And while the blessing of the auspicious day was being recited and the high-souled ones were murmuring their prayers, the sound of feet rushing about was heard, yet no one could be seen.

sanskrit: parasparaṃ ca nakṣatraṃ hanyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ grahair apaśyan sarve te nātmanas tu kathaṃ cana
english: They all saw the constellations being struck again and again by the planets, one against another, yet not one of them could perceive his own.

sanskrit: nadantaṃ pāñcajanyaṃ ca vṛṣṇyandhakaniveśane samantāt pratyavāśyanta rāsabhā dāruṇasvarāḥ
english: And when the conch Pāñcajanya sounded within the dwellings of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, the asses brayed back at it on every side with hideous voices.

sanskrit: evaṃ paśyan hṛṣīkeśaḥ saṃprāptaṃ kālaparyayam trayodaśyām amāvāsyāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā prābravīd idam
english: Seeing thus that the turning of Time had come, Hṛṣīkeśa, when he beheld the new moon fall upon the thirteenth day, spoke these words:

sanskrit: caturdaśī pañcadaśī kṛteyaṃ rāhuṇā punaḥ tadā ca bhārate yuddhe prāptā cādya kṣayāya naḥ
english: "The fourteenth has been made the fifteenth once more by Rāhu; just so it befell in the war of the Bhāratas, and now it has come again for our destruction."

sanskrit: vimṛśann eva kālaṃ taṃ paricintya janārdanaḥ mene prāptaṃ sa ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ varṣaṃ vai keśisūdanaḥ
english: Reflecting upon that hour and pondering it, Janārdana, the slayer of Keśin, judged that the thirty-sixth year had indeed arrived.

sanskrit: putraśokābhisaṃtaptā gāndhārī hatabāndhavā yad anuvyājahārārtā tad idaṃ samupāgatam
english: "That which Gāndhārī, scorched by grief for her sons and bereft of her kinsmen, uttered in her anguish—this has now come to pass.

sanskrit: idaṃ ca tad anuprāptam abravīd yad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ purā vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu dṛṣṭvotpātān sudāruṇān
english: And this too has come about which Yudhiṣṭhira foretold of old, when, the armies drawn up in array, he beheld the dire portents."

sanskrit: ity uktvā vāsudevas tu cikīrṣan satyam eva tat ājñāpayām āsa tadā tīrthayātrām ariṃdama
english: Having said this, Vāsudeva, wishing that very thing to be fulfilled, then gave command for a pilgrimage to the sacred fords, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: aghoṣayanta puruṣās tatra keśavaśāsanāt tīrthayātrā samudre vaḥ kāryeti puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: By Keśava's order men proclaimed there, "You bulls among men shall make a pilgrimage to the sea."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kālī strī pāṇḍurair dantaiḥ praviśya hasatī niśi striyaḥ svapneṣu muṣṇantī dvārakāṃ paridhāvati
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: A black woman with pale teeth, entering by night and laughing, ran about through Dvārakā, snatching away the women in their dreams.

sanskrit: alaṃkārāś ca chatraṃ ca dhvajāś ca kavacāni ca hriyamāṇāny adṛśyanta rakṣobhiḥ subhayānakaiḥ
english: The ornaments, the parasol, the banners, and the coats of mail were seen being carried off by demons most terrible to behold.

sanskrit: tac cāgnidattaṃ kṛṣṇasya vajranābham ayasmayam divam ācakrame cakraṃ vṛṣṇīnāṃ paśyatāṃ tadā
english: And that iron discus of Kṛṣṇa, given by Agni, its hub hard as the thunderbolt, mounted up into the sky as the Vṛṣṇis looked on.

sanskrit: yuktaṃ rathaṃ divyam ādityavarṇaṃ; hayāharan paśyato dārukasya te sāgarasyopariṣṭhād avartan; manojavāś caturo vājimukhyāḥ
english: His divine chariot, yoked and bright as the sun, the horses bore away as Dāruka looked on; those four chief steeds, swift as thought, wheeled away over the surface of the sea.

sanskrit: tālaḥ suparṇaś ca mahādhvajau tau; supūjitau rāmajanārdanābhyām uccair jahrur apsaraso divāniśaṃ; vācaś cocur gamyatāṃ tīrthayātrā
english: The two great banners, the palmyra and the Garuḍa, well honored by Rāma and Janārdana, were borne aloft by the apsarases day and night, and they cried out, "Let the pilgrimage to the sacred fords be made!"

sanskrit: tato jigamiṣantas te vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathāḥ sāntaḥpurās tadā tīrthayātrām aicchan nararṣabhāḥ
english: Then those great chariot-warriors of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, those bulls among men, eager to set out, desired the pilgrimage, taking the women of their households with them.

sanskrit: tato bhojyaṃ ca bhakṣyaṃ ca peyaṃ cāndhakavṛṣṇayaḥ bahu nānāvidhaṃ cakrur madyaṃ māṃsam anekaśaḥ
english: Then the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis prepared food and dainties and drink in abundance and of many kinds, with much wine and flesh of every sort.

sanskrit: tataḥ sīdhuṣu saktāś ca niryayur nagarād bahiḥ yānair aśvair gajaiś caiva śrīmantas tigmatejasaḥ
english: Then, given over to their liquors, those glorious men of fierce splendor went forth from the city by carriages, on horses, and on elephants.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhāse nyavasan yathoddeśaṃ yathāgṛham prabhūtabhakṣyapeyās te sadārā yādavās tadā
english: Then the Yādavas encamped at Prabhāsa, each in his appointed place and as in his own home, with their wives and with abundance of food and drink.

sanskrit: niviṣṭāṃs tān niśamyātha samudrānte sa yogavit jagāmāmantrya tān vīrān uddhavo 'rthaviśāradaḥ
english: When he perceived that they had encamped there by the shore of the sea, Uddhava, skilled in yoga and wise in matters, took his leave of those heroes and departed.

sanskrit: taṃ prasthitaṃ mahātmānam abhivādya kṛtāñjalim jānan vināśaṃ vṛṣṇīnāṃ naicchad vārayituṃ hariḥ
english: As that great soul set forth, saluting him with folded hands, Hari, knowing the destruction of the Vṛṣṇis to be at hand, had no wish to hold him back.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālaparītās te vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathāḥ apaśyann uddhavaṃ yāntaṃ tejasāvṛtya rodasī
english: Then those great chariot-warriors of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, encompassed by Time, beheld Uddhava departing, covering heaven and earth with his radiance.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇārtheṣu yat siddham annaṃ teṣāṃ mahātmanām tad vānarebhyaḥ pradaduḥ surāgandhasamanvitam
english: The food that had been prepared for the brahmins' sake by those high-souled men, reeking of wine, they gave instead to the monkeys.

sanskrit: tatas tūryaśatākīrṇaṃ naṭanartakasaṃkulam prāvartata mahāpānaṃ prabhāse tigmatejasām
english: Then the great carousal of those men of fierce splendor began at Prabhāsa, filled with the sound of a hundred instruments and thronged with players and dancers.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇasya saṃnidhau rāmaḥ sahitaḥ kṛtavarmaṇā apibad yuyudhānaś ca gado babhrus tathaiva ca
english: In Kṛṣṇa's presence Rāma drank, together with Kṛtavarman, and so too did Yuyudhāna, Gada, and Babhru.

sanskrit: tataḥ pariṣado madhye yuyudhāno madotkaṭaḥ abravīt kṛtavarmāṇam avahasyāvamanya ca
english: Then, in the midst of the assembly, Yuyudhāna, made arrogant by drink, addressed Kṛtavarman, mocking and despising him:

sanskrit: kaḥ kṣatriyo manyamānaḥ suptān hanyān mṛtān iva na tan mṛṣyanti hārdikya yādavā yat tvayā kṛtam
english: "What man who counts himself a kṣatriya would slay sleeping men as though they were already dead? That deed of yours, O son of Hṛdika, the Yādavas will not forgive."

sanskrit: ity ukte yuyudhānena pūjayām āsa tad vacaḥ pradyumno rathināṃ śreṣṭho hārdikyam avamanya ca
english: When Yuyudhāna had thus spoken, Pradyumna, best of chariot-warriors, applauded those words, himself also scorning the son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃkruddhaḥ kṛtavarmā tam abravīt nirdiśann iva sāvajñaṃ tadā savyena pāṇinā
english: Then Kṛtavarman, kindled to the height of fury, spoke to him, pointing as it were in contempt with his left hand:

sanskrit: bhūriśravāś chinnabāhur yuddhe prāyagatas tvayā vadhena sunṛśaṃsena kathaṃ vīreṇa pātitaḥ
english: "Bhūriśravas, his arm cut off, sitting fasting unto death upon the field—how was that hero felled by you, by a slaughter most cruel?"

sanskrit: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā keśavaḥ paravīrahā tiryak saroṣayā dṛṣṭyā vīkṣāṃ cakre sa manyumān
english: Hearing these words of his, Keśava, slayer of enemy heroes, full of wrath, cast at him a sidelong glance heavy with anger.

sanskrit: maṇiḥ syamantakaś caiva yaḥ sa satrājito 'bhavat tāṃ kathāṃ smārayām āsa sātyakir madhusūdanam
english: And Sātyaki reminded the slayer of Madhu of the tale of that jewel, the Syamantaka, which had once belonged to Satrājit.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā keśavasyāṅkam agamad rudatī tadā satyabhāmā prakupitā kopayantī janārdanam
english: Hearing this, Satyabhāmā, weeping and enraged, went to Keśava's lap, herself rousing Janārdana to anger.

sanskrit: tata utthāya sakrodhaḥ sātyakir vākyam abravīt pañcānāṃ draupadeyānāṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinoḥ
english: Then Sātyaki rose up in his wrath and spoke—in the name of the five sons of Draupadī, of Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin:

sanskrit: eṣa gacchāmi padavīṃ satyena ca tathā śape sauptike ye ca nihatāḥ suptānena durātmanā
english: "I go now upon the road they took, and thus I swear by the truth: those who were slain in their sleep in the night attack by this evil-souled man—

sanskrit: droṇaputrasahāyena pāpena kṛtavarmaṇā samāptam āyur asyādya yaśaś cāpi sumadhyame
english: by the wicked Kṛtavarman, the ally of Droṇa's son—this very day, O fair-waisted one, his life and his glory shall both be ended!"

sanskrit: itīdam uktvā khaḍgena keśavasya samīpataḥ abhidrutya śiraḥ kruddhaś ciccheda kṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, there in Keśava's very presence, the enraged Sātyaki rushed upon Kṛtavarman with his sword and struck off his head.
